stories.title: Rex and the Not-My-Favorite Bite
stories.outro: See you next time in Sunny Meadow!
stories.moral: You can say what you like without insulting someone else's food.
moralRhyme: Not for me is fine to say,
Kind words leave a friendly way!

youtube.title: Rex and the Not-My-Favorite Bite | Sunny Meadow
youtube.description: Rex made a loud yuck beside Percy's picnic plate. Percy pulled his carefully prepared snack a little closer. A gentle friendship story. You can say what you like without insulting someone else's food. #SunnyMeadow #DreamyDiscoveries

lines.text: Rex made a loud yuck beside Percy's picnic plate.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Percy pulled his carefully prepared snack a little closer.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: That green spread looks absolutely dreadful!
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: It is the pea spread I made for my lunch.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Rex had brought plain bread to their shared picnic.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Percy had offered some spread for him to try.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I have never tried a spread that color before.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: You do not have to taste it if you do not want to.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Rex stared at the spread and wrinkled his nose.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Percy picked up his own small piece of bread.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: It looks like squashed garden grass on a plate.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: I like it. Those words make my lunch feel unwelcome.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Rex tried explaining his dislike even more loudly.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Percy stopped reaching for another little piece.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: But I am allowed not to want green food!
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Yes. I am asking you not to call my food dreadful.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Does Rex have to like every flavor?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Rex looked at his plain bread beside Percy's plate.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He imagined a friend calling his favorite bread awful.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I would not enjoy hearing that about my lunch.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: We can like different things at the same table.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Rex lowered his voice and spoke directly to Percy.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He did not ask his friend to change the snack.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I am sorry I called your food dreadful.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Thank you. It is still fine to choose plain bread.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Rex asked what the spread felt like on bread.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Percy described it without offering another spoonful.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Is it crunchy, or soft like mashed peas?
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Soft. I like mine with this little piece of bread.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Rex decided he wanted one very tiny taste.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Percy let Rex choose the amount for himself.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I am curious now, but only a small dot.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: You can stop after that if you want to.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Rex tasted the small dot on his bread.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He noticed the soft texture before the green pea flavor.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: It feels smooth. I do not like that flavor much.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Then plain bread is still waiting beside your plate.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: What could Rex say about a food he dislikes?
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Rex put the remaining spread back beside Percy.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He kept his words as small as his tasting bite.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: It is not my favorite. Thank you for offering.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: You are welcome. I am glad you told me kindly.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Percy enjoyed his pea spread while Rex ate plain bread.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Neither friend needed the other one's lunch to change.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: We have two different favorite things at this picnic.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: And plenty of room for both on the cloth.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Rex asked Percy about the leaf-shaped bread pieces.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Percy pointed to the rounded ones beside his own plate.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You made these shapes especially for our picnic?
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Yes. Yours are the ones shaped like little dinosaur feet.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Rex smiled at his very plain dinosaur-foot bread.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He thanked Percy for thinking about his favorite snack.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: My bread has excellent toes, even without green spread.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: I thought a dinosaur might appreciate that detail.
lines.speaker: friend

lines.text: Percy offered a pretend shoe fitting for the last piece.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Rex held it above his very large real foot.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: This shoe is much too small for the customer.
lines.speaker: character

lines.text: Then the customer may enjoy eating his footwear.
lines.speaker: friend
